back2basics.concept: International Court of Justice and Genocide
back2basics.text: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations that settles disputes between states according to international law. Genocide is defined as acts intended to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. The ICJ can rule on cases of genocide but relies on the UN Security Council for enforcement, which can be hindered by veto powers of permanent members.

2026-11-25-am-db94562763.deck: On November 19, 2026, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya community. This verdict is significant for UPSC aspirants as it highlights international law on genocide, challenges in enforcement, and regional human rights concerns involving India’s neighbourhood.

back2basics.concept: Space Economy and Private Sector Participation
back2basics.text: The space economy includes all activities related to manufacturing, launching, and using satellites and space technologies. Private sector participation means companies outside the government contribute to building and operating space systems, which can increase innovation, investment, and commercial opportunities. Policy reforms can open government-controlled sectors to private players, enabling faster growth and technological advancement.
